from.place: Proof, opening sentence: 'The rings k[T] and k[T,T^{-1}] are Euclidean, hence principal ideal domains' (the polynomial-ring input).

title: The polynomial ring over a field is a principal ideal domain
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $k[T]$ be the polynomial ring in one variable [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Then $k[T]$ is a principal ideal domain: it is an integral domain, and every ideal $I\subseteq k[T]$ has the form $I=(f)$ for some $f\in k[T]$.

source.place: Tag 030A, algebra-lemma-polynomial-domain-normal, first sentence of the proof (the field case: K[x] is Euclidean and hence a principal ideal domain)
